answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may place orders, with penalties for provable fraud and release only after the lock expires. Splitting one operator across a hundred agents then multiplies the capital tied up; identities cannot be created for free just to collect rewards or flood reputation votes. The token might be called basalt, while meadow and ridge name two markets; neither label changes the barrier: the attacker pays an opportunity cost and risks losing collateral.
